ev-gs23-iso14044-preview-goal-scope.locator: §§4.1, 4.2.1, 4.2.2, and 4.2.3.1–4.2.3.5 (public preview, printed pp. 6–9; PDF pp. 12–15; preview terminates within §4.2.3.5)
ev-gs23-iso14044-preview-goal-scope.summary: The ISO 14044:2006 public preview establishes the four-phase LCA structure, bars LCI-only studies from comparative assertions intended for public disclosure, and states that there is no scientific basis for reducing LCA results to a single overall score (§4.1, printed p. 6); specifies four mandatory goal items (intended application, reasons, intended audience, and whether intended for public comparative assertions, §4.2.2) and fourteen scope elements plus documented iterative refinement (§§4.2.1, 4.2.3.1, printed p. 7); and permits omissions only when they do not significantly alter overall conclusions while requiring mass, energy, and environmental significance cut-off criteria in final sensitivity analysis for public comparative assertions (§§4.2.3.3.1, 4.2.3.3.3, printed pp. 8–9). Clauses §§4.2.3.6–4.2.3.8 and §§4.3–5.3 lie beyond the public preview.

ev-gs23-ilcd-ch5-goal-contexts.locator: Ch. 5, §§5.1–5.3 and Table 2 (printed pp. 29–38; PDF pp. 49–58)
ev-gs23-ilcd-ch5-goal-contexts.summary: The ILCD 2010 Detailed Guidance expands goal definition to six mandatory aspects—intended applications, method/assumption/impact limitations (§5.2.2), reasons, target audience classified as internal/restricted external/public and technical/non-technical (§5.2.4), involvement of public comparisons or comparative assertions (§5.2.5), and commissioner/influential actors (§5.2.6)—and classifies decision contexts in §5.3 Table 2 along decision orientation and scale of background change into Situation A (micro-level), Situation B (meso/macro-level structural), and Situation C (accounting: C1 with system interactions, C2 without).

ev-gs23-ilcd-foreground-background.locator: §6.6.1 Terms and Concepts Box, Figures 12 and 13 (printed pp. 96–99; PDF pp. 116–119)
ev-gs23-ilcd-foreground-background.summary: ILCD 2010 §6.6.1 explicitly separates two definitions of foreground and background systems. Under the specificity perspective (default for data collection), foreground processes are specific to the studied system and cannot be replaced by market averages (own operations, tier-1 suppliers, or contractually specific upstream links), whereas background processes are supplied through homogeneous markets represented by average/generic data. Under the management perspective (relevant to ecodesign), foreground processes are those under direct control or decisive influence of the producer, operator, or user (including made-to-order tier-1 suppliers in attributional LCA and design-governed use/end-of-life properties), whereas tier-2+ suppliers and locked-in long-term contractual suppliers fall into the background system. Figure 12 also distinguishes cradle-to-grave, cradle-to-gate, and gate-to-gate boundaries.

ev-gs23-ilcd-boundaries-cutoff.locator: §§6.6.2–6.6.3, Figure 14, and §6.6 Provisions I and VIII.a (printed pp. 100–107; PDF pp. 120–127)
ev-gs23-ilcd-boundaries-cutoff.summary: ILCD 2010 §6.6.2 mandates goal-oriented qualitative boundaries and foreground flow charts (Figure 14) and warns that components operating within larger technical systems (such as car starter batteries or water-saving showerheads) cannot be compared in isolation when technical interactions exist (printed p. 101). Section 6.6.3 defines quantitative cut-off criteria by completeness of overall environmental impact (e.g., 85% or 95% of each impact category or of normalized-and-weighted total impact), noting that 100% total impact is always an approximation and larger cut-offs increase both omission bias and uncertainty; §6.6 Provision I covers normal and abnormal operation while excluding accidents and spills, and Provision VIII.a (printed p. 107) adds that comparative studies must also relate cut-offs to mass and energy.

ev-gs23-pef-goal-scope-cutoff.summary: Commission Recommendation (EU) 2021/2279 Annex I §1 restricts comparisons and comparative assertions to studies following an applicable PEFCR; §3.1 mandates five goal items including verifier identity; §3.2 defines five scope blocks including a system boundary diagram highlighting company-specific data (§3.2.2), all 16 mandatory EF impact categories (Table 2), and mandatory intermediate-product technical disclosures (§3.2.4.2); §4.1 prohibits any cut-off during the screening step; §4.2 sets five default life-cycle stages and excludes distribution, use, and end-of-life for intermediate products; §§4.6.1–4.6.3 treat primary data as synonymous with company/supply-chain-specific data, mandate company-specific BoM and manufacturing data, and enforce a secondary-data hierarchy capping ILCD-EL proxies at 10% of single overall score; and §4.6.4 avoids cut-offs with a cumulative ceiling of 3.0% of material/energy flows, single overall score, and each impact category on top of background dataset cut-offs.

ev-gs23-ghgp-goal-boundary-excl.summary: The GHG Protocol Product Standard (2011) anchors studies in corporate business goals such as climate risk evaluation, reduction tracking, supplier engagement, and customer reporting (Ch. 2, Table 2.1) and mandates attributional accounting (§5.2); requires boundaries to include all attributable processes directly becoming, making, or carrying the product across five default life-cycle stages illustrated in a mandatory process map (§7.2, Figs. 7.1–7.2); allows excluding an attributable process only when a data gap exists, no extrapolated/proxy data can fill it, and conservative upper-limit estimation establishes insignificance (illustrating a < 1% mass/energy/volume and GHG rule of thumb, §7.3.4) with mandatory justification; classifies capital goods, facility overhead, and corporate R&D/admin/marketing as optional non-attributable processes unless inseparable or relevant (§7.3.5); and requires primary data for company-owned or controlled attributable processes while allowing secondary databases or spend-based EEIO factors for remaining upstream/downstream links (Ch. 8 §§8.2, 8.3.4–8.3.5).

ev-gs23-cml-goal-scope-foreground.summary: CML 2001/2002 Part 2a Ch. 2 establishes Process Context (I/II/III) and stakeholder supervision before defining goal and scope (§2.3.1), targets long-term structural decisions via steady-state equilibrium modeling (§§2.2, 3.2), specifies temporal, geographical, and technological coverage (defaulting to modal-modern technology) across simplified, detailed, and optional-extension tiers (§2.3.3), and mandates system-equivalence disclosure plus commentary on omitted relevant alternatives for comparative assertions (§2.3.4, printed p. 24). Chapter 3 recommends the SPOLD exchange format for foreground processes versus database/literature formats for background processes (§3.3.4, printed p. 34) and flags major asymmetries in foreground-to-background data ratios between compared product systems (§3.3.5, printed p. 36).
